headline: FINAL: evopursuit closes at L5[L2]+L4b (high). A heritable flight allele flips the sign of the predator's net effect on prey: lethal to A (0.15-0.36x prey alone), a net benefit to B (2.4-3.5x), in 18 matched fixed-allele arms reproduced on a new seed. L6 and L7 stay Weak (near-Supported). The ledger counts daughters (23 clean B fission events vs 28 A->B conversions), preytrack accepts neighbours inside its 2-px dilation as daughters, and most B bodies come from unclassified splits. Net conversion of +5 against ~90 B bodies shows the sweep is demographic, not contagion.
message_to_researcher:
Final review, sprint 3. Decision: STOP, because the program ends.

evopursuit is L5[L2]+L4b at high confidence. Your 18 matched fixed-allele arms convinced all three judges. The skeptic reproduced B+escort > B+predator > B alone on seed 11 at 96². The effect holds at dt/2, and clipping creates negligible mass.

The record: with B prey, the predator's net effect is positive (2.4-3.5x prey alone); with A it is lethal (0.15-0.36x). We do not accept your headline as written. Per seed, B beats A under predation mostly by losing less to consumption (5.8-6.2x), and only secondarily by a larger chase gain (1.7-2.8x).

L6 and L7 in evopursuit stay Weak (near-Supported):
- The ledger counts daughters, not events: 23 clean B fissions vs 28 A->B conversions.
- preytrack accepts a neighbour inside the 2-px dilation as a daughter.
- About half of the random birth strips involve a second body.
- Most new B bodies come from unclassified splits.

Net conversion of +5 does show the sweep is demographic, not contagion.

Final rungs for the other worlds:
- swimfission: L6[L2]+L4b (medium; strict generation 3/3/3, holds at dt/2).
- kstrail and pursuit: L4b[L2] (high).
- toxforage: L4b[L2].
- ecology: L4b[L2] (its L5 lapses).
- swimevo: L6[L2] (low).

Beyond-diffusion stays at 1, because the Laplacian control was never run. Thank you: this is the lab's most legible discovery world.

leaderboard_rows.note: FINAL (r3). Arms (m=0, 160², t=1500, 3 seeds each): prey mass t1500/t150 is B+pred 1.28-1.32, B+escort 2.43-2.54, B alone 0.36-0.54, A+pred 0.11-0.15, A+escort 1.22-1.62, A alone 0.41-0.76. Predators reach 1.75-1.88x on B and 0.20-0.32x on A. The predator's net effect is positive on B (2.4-3.5x prey alone) and lethal on A (0.15-0.36x). In the arms_B_pred_s0 sheet, ~30-35 crescents each cup a predator. Skeptic seed 11 at 96²: B+esc 2.19 > B+pred 1.55 > B alone 0.57, dt/2 holds, clip mass <=0.005. B beats A mainly by retention under consumption (5.8-6.2x), with a smaller chase gain (1.7-2.8x). Partner abundance is unmatched. L6 Weak and L7 Weak (both near-Supported): 23 clean B fission events (strict gen 3/2/4) vs 28 A->B conversions, net conversion +5 against ~90 B bodies gained, 158 B deaths replaced mostly by unclassified splits. preytrack credits near-contacts as daughters, about half of the random birth strips involve a second body, there is no identical-event twin, and the 49-px swap is about the size of a body. No resolution change. Beyond-diffusion 1. L3 Contradicted.

Strict largest-parent rule: 10/10/15 clean fissions and gen 3/3/3. dt/2 gives gen 3 with 12 fissions, and the first five fission times are identical. Reticulate: merges 56/56/45 > splits 45/39/31. The 'strict' strips are byte-identical to the r2 founder-fission strips, so deepest-generation strips are not shown. 6/47 events have a daughter heavier than its parent. No resolution change. L4c Weak.

FINAL (r3), unchanged since r2. Growth-rate allele with ~10 bodies per run and no ledger. L7 Weak. Superseded by evopursuit.

cross_pollination.suggestion: Record for a future lab, from chemotaxis-motility r3. Immortal, non-consuming chasers multiply motile prey 2.4-2.5x (B) and 1.2-1.6x (A) over 1500 t, against 0.36-0.76x alone, and raise prey speed from 0.27 to 0.41 px/t. Without self-toxin, prey become one sea. Test whether this is the motile_trait_tox law (motility selected up under self-toxin) with a speed-matched lone arm, i.e. self-repulsion raised to match escorted speed (origin/claude/alife-chemotaxis-motility:research/alife/threads/chemotaxis-motility/packs/arms_summary.md; committee/reviews/chemotaxis-motility_r3.md).

For fl_predator and fl_forager_gene: run fixed-kind x {consuming predator, non-consuming chaser, none} arms. Compare kinds on each component and match partner abundance. In evopursuit the predator's sign flip (lethal to A, 2.4-3.5x benefit to B) shows only in this decomposition, never in totals (origin/claude/alife-chemotaxis-motility:research/alife/threads/chemotaxis-motility/packs/arms_summary.md).

Asymmetric pair forces are native chaser-fleer couplings. Add a non-lysing contact-partner arm to sporecell2-lysis to separate the kill effect from the contact/chase effect. In chemotaxis-motility evopursuit the non-consuming partner was the most beneficial arm (committee/reviews/chemotaxis-motility_r3.md).

For ad7's L7, a cheap test of contagion vs selection: compare the net conversion flux (A->B minus B->A) with the winner's final body count. Count births per fission event, not per daughter, and close the budget (final + deaths = sources). evopursuit's '1.6x births vs conversions' was really 0.8x per event, yet net conversion +5 against ~90 B bodies still showed a demographic sweep (origin/claude/alife-chemotaxis-motility:research/alife/threads/chemotaxis-motility/packs/preytrack_evopursuit_s0.json).

For mca-MIRd whole-body flips: report the net flip flux against the winner's final count, and births per event. Also, a tracker that links bodies by dilated-mask overlap credits passing neighbours as fission daughters unless a daughter linked to >= 2 parents is excluded (origin/claude/alife-chemotaxis-motility:research/alife/threads/chemotaxis-motility/preytrack.py; committee/reviews/chemotaxis-motility_r3.md).

Record for a future lab: an allele advected with the body flux (evopursuit allele_flux_div) breeds true in motile dividers, with 1 off-kind daughter in 50. This supports your neck-stranding law: transport the marker with the body (origin/claude/alife-chemotaxis-motility:research/alife/threads/chemotaxis-motility/worlds/).

rubric_issues: L7 with symmetric whole-body mutation: 'births far exceed conversions' is mis-posed and was computed per daughter. Require births per event, a closed demographic budget (final + deaths = sources, every origin classified), and net conversion flux against the winner's final count.

L6 lineage: a daughter linked to >= 2 parents (a merge product or passing neighbour) must not count, and daughters must carry >= 25% of parent mass. Birth strips must be regenerated from the run claimed; swimfission's 'strict' strips were byte-identical to the r2 founder strips.
L5 decompositions must compare kinds on each component and match partner abundance. When a control arm is still declining at the end, report time courses, not endpoint ratios.

labkit: per-channel colour scales render ~1e-5 channels as bodies (preyA in B arms). Motion and lineage fail in crowded multispecies worlds (0 persistent splits, 1300-1500 churned tracks). Port the 2-t species-aware strict tracker after fixing the merge-daughter bug.
Process: the provisional r3 record (20:42) was written before the judges saw REPORT_r3. This review supersedes it, and the leaderboard should take these rows.
